title: The Ghost of Ghat 9
logline: A bandit robs the monsoon mail train at a bend nobody can reach in time — unless the timetable itself is lying.
artStyle: Isometric 1950s hill railway: wet slate, rust and teak, lantern light through rain, muted teal and ochre, 2:1 dimetric.

cast.name: Inspector Rane
cast.persona: Soaked khaki and a notebook with swollen pages. Patient to the point of rudeness, asks the obvious question twice, and writes down the answer both times.

cast.name: Station Master Dalvi
cast.persona: Brass buttons and an umbrella he never opens. Helpful to a fault, quotes the timetable as scripture, and cannot see that an average over a route says nothing about any single moment of it.

acts.title: The Alibi
acts.goal: Dalvi's book puts the guard six kilometres up the ghat in ten minutes. Show him what that would take.

prediction.question: Dalvi says the guard walked 6 km up the ghat in 10 minutes. Before you compute anything — is that possible?
options: Yes, uphill is slow but 6 km is a short distance
No, that implies a speed no one walks
Only if he ran the whole way

acts.explainAfter: Average speed is total distance over total time, and it does not care how the walk felt. 6 km in 10 minutes is 36 km/h. A person tops out near 25 km/h on flat ground for seconds at a time, so it is the timing that is wrong, not the walker. This is why an average is evidence: it can be impossible.

spec.win: claimedSpeed >= impliedSpeed - 1 && claimedSpeed <= impliedSpeed + 1 && impliedSpeed > walkMaxKmh

band.label: Green is what a person can actually walk. Dalvi's timings land outside it — that is the lie.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Dalvi
dialogue.line: The guard left at ten past and signed in at twenty past. Six kilometres. It is all written down.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Dalvi
dialogue.line: By me. As it has been for nineteen years.

dialogue.speaker: Inspector Rane
dialogue.line: Then set the board to what your own timings imply, and we shall see what nineteen years is worth.

signed-timetable.speaker: Station Master Dalvi
lines: Guard Phadke, departed Ghat 9 — ten past the hour.
Signed in at Kanhe cabin — twenty past. Six kilometres of ghat path between them.
Signed, R. Dalvi, Station Master. Nineteen years of them, in this same hand.

beat.won: Dalvi sits down very suddenly. The book stays open on the desk.
beat.lost: Dalvi folds his arms. "Nineteen years, Inspector."
beat.speaker: Inspector Rane

acts.title: The Runaway
acts.goal: You have a brake and nothing else. Ride her down the grade and stop her inside the siding — short of the water tank.

prediction.question: You move the marker 10 m further down the grade. The stopping distance…
options: Shrinks — braking starts later so there is less left to lose
Stays the same — the brakes do not know where they are
Grows — the train has longer to pick up speed

acts.explainAfter: Once the brakes bite, the distance to stop depends on how fast you were going and how hard you can brake — not on where you started braking. Moving the marker moves the whole stop; it does not shorten it. That is v² = u² + 2as read backwards: double the speed and you quadruple the distance.

visual.xLabel: time since she was let go (s)

band.label: Braking later moves the whole stop down the hill. It never makes it shorter.

dialogue.speaker: Inspector Rane
dialogue.line: The siding ends at the water tank. Overrun it and we are both in the gorge.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Dalvi
dialogue.line: Brake at the top, Inspector. One always brakes at the top.

dialogue.speaker: Inspector Rane
dialogue.line: At the top she is still doing sixteen. Let us find out what sixteen costs.

bindings.label: brake
bindings.prompt: release the brakes and ride her down

beat.won: She comes to rest with the tank still dry. Dalvi says nothing at all.
beat.lost: Water everywhere and the siding points bent. Rane does not look at you.
beat.speaker: Inspector Rane

acts.title: The Zipline
acts.goal: The bandit is on the far ledge and walking. Put the mail across before he reaches it.

prediction.question: You double the forward speed and keep the upward speed the same. The satchel…
options: Stays in the air twice as long
Lands twice as far, in the same flight time
Lands twice as far and twice as late

acts.explainAfter: Horizontal and vertical motion do not talk to each other. Gravity only ever works on the vertical, so the time in the air is set by the upward speed and the drop — and the forward speed just decides how much ground that time buys you. Height buys seconds; speed spends them.

spec.win: landX >= ledgeNear && landX <= ledgeFar && flight <= banditEta

band.label: Upward speed sets how long it flies. He is walking the whole time it is up there.

dialogue.speaker: Inspector Rane
dialogue.line: The ledge is twenty-six metres out and eleven below. He is on it already, and walking.

dialogue.speaker: Inspector Rane
dialogue.line: Then he will watch it come down at his leisure.

beat.won: The satchel hits the ledge a clear stride ahead of him. He turns and runs.
beat.lost: He picks it up without breaking stride and is gone into the trees.
beat.speaker: Inspector Rane

twist: There was no bandit on the ghat that night until Dalvi needed one. He wrote the timings himself, signed them himself, and read them back to you himself — nineteen years of a hand that nobody had ever once checked.
